title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant F

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: Level A1-A2. Three short personal questions asked one after another. 30 seconds for each answer. No preparation time. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant F - Part 1.1 (Home, neighbourhood and interests)
Level A1-A2. Scored items 1, 2 and 3 (marked together, 0-5).

[Stage direction: check the candidate's name and seat the candidate. There is NO preparation time in this part. Time each answer at 30 seconds and stop the candidate politely when the 30 seconds are up.]

EXAMINER (read aloud, exactly as written):
"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[Stage direction: play the chime, then ask question 1.]

QUESTION 1 (scored item 1 - 30 SECONDS)
"Where do you live - in a big city, a small town or a village?"
[Stage direction: allow 30 seconds. Then say "Thank you." and move straight on.]

QUESTION 2 (scored item 2 - 30 SECONDS)
"Tell me about your home. Which room do you like most, and why?"
[Stage direction: allow 30 seconds. Then say "Thank you." and move straight on.]

QUESTION 3 (scored item 3 - 30 SECONDS)
"Tell me about something new you have started doing recently - a sport, a hobby or a class."
[Stage direction: allow 30 seconds. Then say "Thank you. Now we are going to look at some photographs." and go straight to Part 1.2.]

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: Level B1. Two photographs on one theme. Question 4 asks you to compare and describe the two pictures - 45 seconds. Questions 5 and 6 ask for your opinion - 30 seconds each. No preparation time.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant F - Part 1.2 (City life and housing)
Level B1. Scored items 4, 5 and 6 (marked together, 0-5). NO preparation time.

[Stage direction: place the two photographs in front of the candidate, side by side, before you speak. If no printed photographs are available, read the two descriptions below aloud, slowly, and leave them on the desk in writing.]

[PICTURE 1: a narrow street of low, old two-storey houses with painted wooden gates and flat roofs; washing hangs on a line between two walls, an elderly woman sits on a bench beside a door and two children ride bicycles past a small corner shop; a tree grows out of a gap in the pavement; late afternoon sunlight.]

[PICTURE 2: a wide paved courtyard between three brand-new glass-fronted apartment towers of about twenty floors; identical balconies rise in neat rows, a young couple lift shopping bags out of a car at the entrance to an underground garage, and a security barrier and a line of thin newly-planted trees stand at the edge; grey overcast morning.]

EXAMINER (read aloud, exactly as written):
"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

QUESTION 4 - compare and describe (scored item 4 - 45 SECONDS)
[Stage direction: play the chime. Allow 45 seconds. The candidate should describe both pictures and say how they differ. If the candidate stops after only a few seconds, prompt once: "And the other photograph?" At 45 seconds say "Thank you."]

QUESTION 5 - opinion (scored item 5 - 30 SECONDS)
"Which of these two places would you prefer to live in, and why?"
[Stage direction: allow 30 seconds. Then say "Thank you."]

QUESTION 6 - opinion (scored item 6 - 30 SECONDS)
"What is the most important thing for a family to think about when they choose a new home?"
[Stage direction: allow 30 seconds. Then say "Thank you. That is the end of Part one." Collect the photographs and go to Part 2.]

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: Level B2. One picture and three questions, given to you at the same time. You have 1 minute to think and 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. You are NOT required to describe the picture - it is there only to suggest the topic.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant F - Part 2 (City life and housing)
Level B2. Scored item 7 (0-5). ONE picture and THREE questions, all presented AT ONCE.
1 minute preparation, then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together.

[Stage direction: put the picture and the three questions in front of the candidate at the same moment, then read the instructions. Give paper and a pencil for notes.]

EXAMINER (read aloud, exactly as written):
"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[PICTURE: a half-finished housing development on the edge of a city - three concrete apartment blocks with cranes still standing over them, a muddy unfinished road running in front of them, and in the near corner of the frame one old single-storey house with a vegetable garden and a low fence, clearly still lived in, surrounded on three sides by the building site.]

[Stage direction: tell the candidate, in these words: "You do not have to describe the picture. It is only there to help you think about the topic."]

THE THREE QUESTIONS (give all three together, in writing if possible, and read them aloud once):
1. "Tell me about a time when you or your family moved to a different home or to a different part of town."
2. "How did that move change your daily life - your journey to work or to study, and the people around you?"
3. "In general, what makes people decide to leave one neighbourhood and move to another?"

[Stage direction: start the one minute of preparation now and say nothing during it. At the end of the minute say "Your minute is finished.", play the chime and start timing two minutes.]
[Stage direction: if the candidate stops before the two minutes are over, prompt once with the next unanswered question, for example "And my third question?" At two minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of Part two."]

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
Level C1. One topic statement with a FOR list and an AGAINST list, three points in each.
Choose TWO points from the FOR list and TWO points from the AGAINST list and give a balanced argument representing both sides of the topic.
You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant F - Part 3 (City life - public space)
Level C1. Scored item 8 (0-6). ONE topic with two lists. 1 minute preparation, 2 minutes speaking.

[Stage direction: show the candidate the topic and both lists together, in writing, then read the instructions. Give paper and a pencil for notes.]

EXAMINER (read aloud, exactly as written):
"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

TOPIC:
"Every city should keep its parks, playgrounds and sports grounds free for all residents to use, paid for out of local taxes."

FOR (choose TWO):
1. Free open space is the cheapest form of public health: people who can walk, run and play without paying stay healthier for longer.
2. A park with no ticket desk is one of the few places where residents of very different incomes still meet as equals.
3. Children and teenagers with nowhere free and safe to go simply gather in car parks and stairwells instead.

AGAINST (choose TWO):
1. The cost falls on every taxpayer, including the many residents who never set foot in a park from one year to the next.
2. Without entrance fees or memberships there is no reliable income for repairs, and changing rooms, courts and play equipment slowly fall apart.
3. Space that nobody pays for is space nobody feels responsible for, and neglected grounds are quickly given over to litter and late-night nuisance.

[Stage direction: start the one minute of preparation now and say nothing during it. At the end of the minute say "Your minute is finished.", play the chime and start timing two minutes.]
[Stage direction: if the candidate presents only one side, prompt once: "And the other side of the topic?" At two minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]
